reuse.why: Introduces one shared link guard used by all providers, but the Fintegra link and download functions are wholesale copies of the SimpleFin/Akahu ones and the takeover path re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a ~90-line copy of linkSimpleFinAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions verbatim, and the unlink column reset duplicates unlinkAccount.

placement.why: Guard, handler, download function and server path live in the same modules where the tree puts the other providers' equivalents.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; the desktop-client edits are the minimum forced by the provider union, plus release notes and a test.

maintainability.why: A helper named assertBankAccountNotLinked now also rejects closed accounts and silently unlinks other accounts, and a sixth near-identical link function and download function grow the per-provider copy pattern.

bypasses_abstraction.where: app.ts assertBankAccountNotLinked: the replaceExistingLink branch re-implements the column reset of unlinkAccount instead of sharing it (e.g. extracting the local-detach part).

disguised_duplication.where: The duplicated blocks (linkFintegraAccount vs linkSimpleFinAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions vs downloadAkahuTransactions, unlink reset) are verbatim copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked (app.ts): created in step 1, then given a closed-account check (step 3) and a replaceExistingLink parameter with a mutating unlink branch (step 4), so an assert now performs writes; the unlink branch bypasses unlinkAccount.
